subject: maths
pattern: Continuity and Differentiability carries 10-12 marks in the Karnataka 2nd PUC maths paper: 1-mark definitions and quick derivatives, 2-mark implicit, logarithmic and parametric differentiation, 3-mark proofs such as differentiability implies continuity, Rolle's theorem or MVT verification and second-order derivative relations, and a 5-mark question on finding constants for continuity or a second derivative. Examiners expect the limit conditions (LHL = RHL = f(c)) and every differentiation step to be shown.

questions.q: Define continuity of a function $f$ at a point $x=c$.
questions.answer: A function $f$ is continuous at $x=c$ if $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to c}f(x)=f(c)$, i.e. the left hand limit, the right hand limit and the value of the function at $c$ all exist and are equal.
By the chain rule, $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=e^{\sin x}\cdot\dfrac{d}{dx}(\sin x)=e^{\sin x}\cos x$.
If $f:[a,b]\to\mathbb{R}$ is continuous on $[a,b]$, differentiable on $(a,b)$ and $f(a)=f(b)$, then there exists at least one point $c\in(a,b)$ such that $f'(c)=0$.
Take logarithms: $\log y=x\log x$. Differentiate: $\dfrac1y\dfrac{dy}{dx}=x\cdot\dfrac1x+\log x=1+\log x$. Hence $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=x^x(1+\log x)$.

questions.q: Find the value of $k$ for which $f(x)=\begin{cases}kx+1,&x\le5\\3x-5,&x>5\end{cases}$ is continuous at $x=5$.
questions.answer: LHL $=\lim_{x\to5^-}(kx+1)=5k+1$. RHL $=\lim_{x\to5^+}(3x-5)=10$. $f(5)=5k+1$. For continuity LHL $=$ RHL $=f(5)$: $5k+1=10$, so $k=\dfrac95$.

questions.q: Prove that every differentiable function is continuous.
questions.answer: Let $f$ be differentiable at $x=c$, so $f'(c)=\lim_{x\to c}\dfrac{f(x)-f(c)}{x-c}$ exists. For $x\neq c$, $f(x)-f(c)=\dfrac{f(x)-f(c)}{x-c}\cdot(x-c)$. Taking limits as $x\to c$: $\lim[f(x)-f(c)]=f'(c)\cdot0=0$. Hence $\lim_{x\to c}f(x)=f(c)$, so $f$ is continuous at $c$. The converse is not true, e.g. $|x|$ at $0$.

questions.q: Differentiate $x^{\sin x}+(\sin x)^{\cos x}$ with respect to $x$.
questions.answer: Let $u=x^{\sin x}$, $v=(\sin x)^{\cos x}$. $\log u=\sin x\log x\Rightarrow\dfrac{du}{dx}=x^{\sin x}\left[\dfrac{\sin x}{x}+\cos x\log x\right]$. $\log v=\cos x\log\sin x\Rightarrow\dfrac{dv}{dx}=(\sin x)^{\cos x}\left[\cos x\cot x-\sin x\log\sin x\right]$. Hence $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{du}{dx}+\dfrac{dv}{dx}$.

Put $x=\tan\theta$, so $\theta=\tan^{-1}x$ with $|\theta|<\tfrac\pi4$. Then $\dfrac{2x}{1+x^2}=\sin2\theta$, so $y=\sin^{-1}(\sin2\theta)=2\theta=2\tan^{-1}x$. Therefore $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{2}{1+x^2}$.

$y_1=e^{a\sin^{-1}x}\cdot\dfrac{a}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$, so $\sqrt{1-x^2}\,y_1=ay$. Differentiate: $\sqrt{1-x^2}\,y_2-\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}y_1=ay_1$. Multiply by $\sqrt{1-x^2}$: $(1-x^2)y_2-xy_1=a\sqrt{1-x^2}\,y_1=a\cdot ay=a^2y$. Hence $(1-x^2)y_2-xy_1-a^2y=0$.

questions.q: Verify the Mean Value Theorem for $f(x)=x^2-4x-3$ on $[1,4]$.
questions.answer: $f$ is a polynomial, hence continuous on $[1,4]$ and differentiable on $(1,4)$. $f(1)=-6$, $f(4)=-3$. $\dfrac{f(4)-f(1)}{4-1}=\dfrac{-3+6}{3}=1$. $f'(c)=2c-4=1\Rightarrow c=\dfrac52\in(1,4)$. Hence the MVT is verified.

questions.q: Find the values of $a$ and $b$ such that $f(x)=\begin{cases}5,&x\le2\\ax+b,&2<x<10\\21,&x\ge10\end{cases}$ is a continuous function.
questions.answer: Continuity at $x=2$: LHL $=5$, RHL $=2a+b$, so $2a+b=5$ ... (i). Continuity at $x=10$: LHL $=10a+b$, RHL $=f(10)=21$, so $10a+b=21$ ... (ii). Subtract (i) from (ii): $8a=16$, so $a=2$. Then $b=5-4=1$. Hence $a=2$ and $b=1$.
